answer.rationale: p99 latency is 5x target on the write path during peak settlement traffic. The release cannot be rolled back due to compliance constraints. Memory_b3 demonstrates that provisioning headroom before high-load periods absorbs surge without queue depth degradation. Adding capacity directly addresses the write path bottleneck, is reversible if ineffective, and aligns with the proven pattern of headroom absorption during peak load. Circuit breakers (b4) and read routing (b5) don't address write-path saturation; failover (b2) risks settlement consistency; rollback is ruled out. Capacity addition is the highest-leverage single intervention available.
